name: Secondary Button
propertyCopy: Set the button’s size, content, corners and label.
guide: Component Guide Human View Machine View Overview Secondary Button is the supporting-action counterpart to Primary - an outlined, unfilled button used for the alternate or less urgent action in the same view, most often placed directly beside a Primary Button. When to Use The alternate action next to a Primary Button - Cancel beside Save, Back beside Continue. Actions that matter but aren't the main goal of the screen - Preview, Edit, Export, View Details. Anywhere a bordered, medium-emphasis button reads better than a full fill - toolbars, card footers, dialog footers. When Not to Use The single most important action on the screen - use Primary instead, so there is still exactly one highest-emphasis control. Irreversible actions - use Destructive so danger is communicated by color as well as position. Dense, repeated row actions - use Ghost or Tertiary, since Secondary's border still carries meaningful visual weight at scale. Best Practices Pair it with a Primary Button rather than using it alone as a screen's only action. Keep its border and label weight consistent everywhere it's the "other" choice, so users learn what a bordered button means across the product. Avoid placing two Secondary buttons side by side for genuinely different actions - if neither is more important, consider Tertiary or Ghost instead. Do and Don't Do PublishSave draft Secondary sits beside one Primary, offering a real alternative without competing for the first glance. Don't Delete account A Secondary carrying a destructive, high-stakes action undersells its own consequence. Give it Destructive's weight instead. Accessibility Same native <button> semantics as Primary - keyboard reachable, Enter/Space activates it. Border and text color meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast against the panel background in both themes. Focus ring is a visible 2px outline, independent of hover styling.
